profile.behavior: Moves with quick flights and short hops through low vegetation, gleaning insects from leaves and branch tips and often hanging upside down; males sing from exposed perches.
field_marks: Bright yellow head and underparts with an olive-green back
Thin black eyeline passing through the dark eye; typically grayer and less distinct in females
Sharp, pointed black bill that appears relatively substantial for a small warbler
Blue-gray wings crossed by two prominent white wing bars
Short tail with white outer-feather markings and white undertail coverts
Small, well-proportioned body with slender legs
profile.habitat: Breeds in shrublands, brushy fields, thickets, and forest edges. During migration it uses open woodland, scrub, gardens, and parks; nonbreeding habitat includes evergreen or tropical deciduous forest edges, scrub, and hedgerows.

The specimen has one head, one bill, one visible eye, one tail, two convincingly attached legs with complete gripping feet, and a coherent folded near-side wing; the far-side wing is naturally occluded by the strict side-profile pose.

Every visible identification, habitat, behavior, taxonomy, palette, and measurement statement matches the proposed profile. The 11–12 cm length, 9 g weight, and 15 cm wingspan set is directly supported by All About Birds for both sexes.
